transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anita Shah (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (CTO, Aurelius), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Priya Menon (Security), Ethan Zhao (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick recap at top, may be rough

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we were asked to focus on networking for the private VPC deployment and runtime perf implications, so Carlos and Anita will dig into the technical pieces.
00:13 Sana: Thanks Maya, we want to understand the tradeoffs between PrivateLink and VPC peering mainly for data path and egress. Also curious about how KV cache and batching behave when the inference runtime is in our VPC.
00:29 Carlos: Cool, quick agenda 	6 PrivateLink architecture, NAT/egress for model pulls and metrics, subnet sizing and autoscale, DNS split-horizon, and then runtime notes: KV cache locality, batching latency, and quantization effects.
00:47 Liam: A couple constraints up front: our security team blocks outbound ranges except through a centralized NAT, and we have strict host-based firewall rules. Also we run cross-account peering for some services today.
01:02 Anita: Right, so for PrivateLink we present an interface endpoint in your account, the data path goes over AWS backbone via the endpoint. That means we avoid peering, and you can keep more restrictive routing. Latency is often a bit lower than internet egress but comparable to peering depending on AZ locality.
01:22 Ethan: When you say "present an interface endpoint" 	6 is that cross-account? Like how do we manage acceptances?
01:29 Carlos: It's an AWS interface endpoint that we provision on our side and you accept the endpoint in your account or we provide a CloudFormation to do cross-account. The endpoint sits in your subnet and then traffic to the service uses the ENI in that subnet.
01:46 Priya: From compliance, we want to ensure no unintended internet egress and that all data stays in-account unless explicitly allowed. How is certs and mTLS handled?
01:54 Maya: We support mTLS over the PrivateLink connection; certificates can be managed via customer KMS or Redwood-managed certs depending on the deployment. We'll send the PKI checklist.
02:06 Liam: OK, but thinking about model downloads and image pulls 	6 those can be big. If the runtime needs to pull model shards or quantized artifacts at startup, will that go over the same interface?
02:18 Carlos: Typically yes, model pull is done via our artifact service. For Private deployments we can mirror artifacts into your S3 (we can sync) or we can allow the runtime to pull via PrivateLink. If you want zero internet, mirroring into your S3 or pre-loading to the nodes is safest. That avoids NAT bandwidth spikes.
02:38 Sana: Pre-loading sounds promising. For autoscale, though, new nodes might spin up and need models 	6 we have bursts. How do we avoid cold-start transfers impacting latency and cost?
02:49 Anita: Two patterns: 1) pre-warm a small pool of nodes with pinned models (warm pool) and 2) use a fast local caching layer 	6 Redwood's KV cache can be hosted on the same node or in a low-latency subnet. Cold-starts can be mitigated by model warmers and smarter orchestration.
03:07 Liam: So KV cache locality 	6 is the cache per-GPU node or shared across nodes? If shared, we worry about cross-AZ hop latency.
03:16 Carlos: Good Q. By default we colocate the KV cache inside the same process on the GPU node (local KV for reduced latency). We also support a shared cache tier for very bursty workloads, but shared caches add network hops and can increase p50/p90 by a small amount. For the lowest latency we recommend local KV plus the warm pool.
03:39 Ethan: What about batching 	6 we batch on the runtime to improve throughput, but batch size increases tail latency. Any guidance for tail-sensitive endpoints?
03:47 Carlos: We have adaptive batching policies 	6 you can set an SLO for tail latency and the runtime will limit batch sizes to meet it, or use priority queues for low-latency requests. For private VPC, ensure the request ingress path into the subnet has sufficient throughput and low jitter.
04:05 Sana: How big of a diff do we see with quantized models? We want to reduce GPU RAM usage but worry about quality.
04:13 Anita: Generally int8 or 4-bit quantization reduces runtime memory and increases throughput, often lowering p99 latency due to better fit on GPU caches. But quantization noise can affect quality; Redwood suggests A/B runs on a sample eval set. We can run those with your prompts in the bench.
04:35 Priya: DNS 	6 we use split-horizon DNS. If the PrivateLink endpoint resolves differently inside our VPC, do we need to change conditional forwarding?
04:44 Carlos: You can keep split-horizon. For interface endpoints you get private DNS option; when enabled the service name resolves to the endpoint's private IPs. If you want to control resolution, disable private DNS and create your own CNAME or route records. We'll put sample configs.
05:05 Liam: NAT and egress 	6 our infra team wants all egress through a central NAT with proxy for inspection. PrivateLink avoids egress but model pulls might still go out. Do you support S3 mirroring so we keep everything inside?
05:18 Maya: Yes, we support artifact mirroring to your S3 and you can restrict runtime to only talk to S3 and the PrivateLink endpoint. That keeps all traffic internal.
05:25 Ethan: Any known perf delta when using PrivateLink vs peering? We run critical low-latency inference (around 20-30ms p50 target).
05:34 Carlos: In our tests, PrivateLink often introduces low single-digit ms overhead vs peering when cross-AZ is involved, but design matters. If both ENI and runtime are in same AZ/subnet, overhead is minimal. For 20-30ms targets you need colocated nodes, local KV, and small adaptive batches.
06:00 Sana: For autoscaling across subnets, route tables 	6 do you recommend dedicated inference subnets per AZ?
06:08 Anita: Yes, dedicated inference subnets per AZ sized for expected max nodes. Keep ENI resources and IP allocation in mind; we recommend leaving a buffer for autoscaled nodes and using secondary IPs on ENIs.
06:22 Liam: What about security groups 	6 do we need a special SG for the interface endpoint?
06:28 Carlos: The interface endpoint ENI will have SGs 	6 treat it like any service; lock down to your runtime subnets and management IPs. Also ensure NACLs allow the ephemeral ports we use (we'll provide port list).
06:41 Priya: KMS integration 	6 we need to ensure CMKs meet our policy and key access logs are available. How do you integrate with customer KMS?
06:50 Maya: We can support customer-managed CMKs for data-at-rest encryption and signings. The runtime can be configured to use your KMS via IAM roles; we'll document the necessary policies.
07:05 Ethan: A nit 	6 when batching is enabled, is the KV cache keyed by request prefix or chat session? We worry about cache thrash across tenants.
07:15 Carlos: KV cache keys are session/tokenized prefix-aware; you can scope caches per-customer/tenant. We also support cache tenant isolation and TTLs to avoid thrash.
07:30 Sana: What about model fallback and rollouts in private VPC? If we pin to a version, can Redwood still roll forward in case of outage?
07:40 Maya: You can pin model versions; for resilience we recommend a fallback policy that points to a compatible variant in Redwood-managed region if the primary fails. That fallback can be route-limited and audited. In Private deployments you control whether to allow automatic fallback.
07:58 Liam: Do you have recommendations for subnet MTU or high-throughput tuning?
08:05 Carlos: For large model transfers, higher MTU helps. Also tune ENI bandwidth and use enhanced networking (SR-IOV) on nodes. We'll include a perf tuning checklist.
08:25 Anita: On quantization and runtime 	6 some kernels execute faster when sequence lengths are short; if your workload has variable context sizes the runtime will choose kernels adaptively. That affects throughput.
08:40 Ethan: Any guidance around multi-tenant VPCs vs single-tenant? We are thinking single VPC for all inference but segregated subnets per team.
08:50 Carlos: Single VPC is fine with good tenant isolation, but for strict compliance a single-tenant VPC per business unit is easier. Performance-wise, single VPC with subnet isolation is fine, as long as you size subnets and ENIs.
09:10 Sana: OK let's talk concrete bench expectations 	6 what metrics will you provide?
09:18 Carlos: We'll provide p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, bytes transferred for model pulls, and tail latency breakdowns by network hop and batching queuing time.
09:33 Maya: We'll run two bench configs: 1) quantized model (4-bit) pinned on warm pool, 2) float32 model with shared cache. We'll compare quality on your eval set.
09:45 Liam: For bench we can open a test account or you can run in our staging VPC 	6 what's preferred?
09:52 Carlos: Either works. For network realism run in your staging VPC with our PrivateLink endpoint so we capture NAT and proxy effects. If that's slow to provision, we can run in a Redwood-hosted test VPC but results may differ slightly.
10:10 Priya: Please include a list of required audit logs and SAML attributes for SSO.
10:16 Maya: We'll send a security packet with SOC2 artifacts, SAML/SSO guide, and KMS policies.
10:22 Sana: Great. Any blockers on Redwood side to doing PrivateLink in our account?
10:28 Carlos: No blockers 	6 we just need the endpoint acceptance, CIDR lists, and security contact. Also confirm if you require Bring-Your-Own-ENI permissions or we can create the ENI for the interface endpoint.
10:45 Ethan: Quick question on fallback bandwidth 	6 if we allow fallback to Redwood-managed region, does that cross your interconnects or public internet?
10:52 Maya: That would go over backbone/private inter-region links where available; otherwise it falls back to AWS public interconnect. We'll clarify in the network checklist.
11:08 Sana: Ok that was useful. Recap and next steps?
11:15 Maya: Action items: we send checklist and network diagram; you supply CIDRs and NAT config; we schedule bench run for week of 4/19; we run quantized vs float runs and share results.
11:28 Liam: Sounds good. We'll aim to get the VPC details by 4/16.
11:35 Priya: We'll follow up with SOC2 contact.
11:40 Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with attachments and the CFN templates.
